title: Vegetable Biryani
subtitle: Fragrant basmati rice layered with spiced vegetables and saffron
excerpt: Biryani is a layered rice dish from the Indian subcontinent. This vegetable version builds flavour at each stage: spiced vegetables, partially cooked rice, then a final oven bake that lets everything steam together.
sourceNotes: Biryani has Persian roots and spread across South Asia with the Mughal Empire. The dum cooking method, where rice and filling are sealed and steamed together, is central to all versions.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook the vegetable base a day ahead and refrigerate. Partially boil the rice fresh before assembling.
recipe.temperatureNote: Fan 160C / Gas 4. For the final oven bake.

content.text: The rice goes into the pot only 70 percent cooked. It finishes cooking in the sealed pot with the vegetables, absorbing all the spiced steam. Do not skip the partial cooking step or the rice will be undercooked in the centre.

Preheat the oven. Heat the ghee in a large ovenproof stockpot over medium heat. Add the sliced onion and cook for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden and beginning to crisp at the edges. Remove half the onion and set aside for topping.
Add the cumin seeds to the pot and fry for 30 seconds. Add the garlic and ginger. Stir for 2 minutes.
Add the ground spices. Stir for 1 minute. Add the potato and carrot. Coat in the spice mixture and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the tinned tomatoes and 100ml of water. Simmer for 10 minutes until the potato is half-cooked. Stir in the peas and season well.

Partially cook the rice: bring the vegetable stock to the boil in a separate pan. Add the drained rice and cook for 5 minutes until 70 percent done (it should have a white dot in the centre when bitten). Drain.
Layer the par-cooked rice over the vegetable base in the pot. Drizzle the saffron water over the top. Scatter the reserved caramelised onion over.
Cover tightly with a lid (or seal with foil then a lid). Bake for 20 minutes. Remove from the oven and leave sealed for 5 more minutes before opening. Fluff gently with a fork.

items.symptom: The rice is undercooked in the centre.
items.cause: The rice was too raw before layering, or the pot was not sealed tightly.
items.fix: Return to the oven sealed for another 10 minutes.

items.symptom: The bottom layer has caught and scorched.
items.cause: The vegetable base was too dry or the heat was too high.
items.fix: Add a splash of water to the base before layering next time.

items.symptom: The saffron colour has not spread through the rice.
items.cause: Not enough liquid was used to dissolve the saffron.
items.fix: Dissolve saffron in a full 4 tablespoons of warm water.
